subject: Regal Health pilot: air-gapped on-prem feasibility & product constraints
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Regal Health pilot request — initial ask + constraints (air-gapped)

Team —

Quick context: Regal Health (Alice Wong) reached out asking for a 3-month, air-gapped on-prem pilot of Redwood for an internal clinical-assistant workflow. They explicitly require:
- No egress of PII or clinical notes from their network
- Monthly model updates via signed bundle (no live pull from hosted registry)
- Hardware to be hosted in their data center (NVMe-backed nodes, 2x A10G equivalent GPUs)
- Minimal telemetry; only opt-in, encrypted health pings to a customer-managed endpoint

Attached their one-page ask (regal_pilot_rq_v1.pdf) and a quick sketch from Alice. High-level asks from Product/Customer: ability to ship a sealed runtime image + update mechanism, clear guidance on which model variants are supported offline, and a rough ops/resourcing estimate so Procurement can proceed.

As next steps I need:
1) Security: confirm if the sealed image + offline updates align with our KMS/HSM approach and SOC2 scope (Stephanie)
2) Infra: rough sizing and any special packaging or kernel/drivers required for an on-prem appliance (Marcus)
3) Runtime/serving: list of supported models and constraints (quantization, KV cache persistence, latency expectations when run offline) (Karthik)
4) Sales: help draft a short pilot scope and minimal SOW for Procurement (Grace)

Can you each reply with your top 3 risks and one mitigator by EOD tomorrow? I'll consolidate before the 3pm sync with Alice on Thursday.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Regal Health pilot request — initial ask + constraints (air-gapped)

Jordan / team —

Thanks for flagging. Top risks from Security/Compliance:

1) Key management and trust model — if we deliver a sealed image that needs to be updated monthly, we need an offline signing and verification protocol that ties into the customer's KMS or an HSM-backed signing key we both trust. Mitigator: prototype an "offline bundle" format with signed manifests and a verify-only lightweight verifier; run a short threat model with Regal.

2) Audit evidence for SOC2 / HIPAA questions — Regal will want evidence of change logs, who pushed updates, and that telemetry was disabled by default. Mitigator: produce a hardened checklist + a supporting evidence pack (logs, checksums, release notes) as part of the pilot artifacts.

3) Telemetry and data leakage — risk of accidental network callbacks. Mitigator: default to zero outbound queues; support manual, customer-controlled health pings to a customer-managed endpoint over mTLS.

Other notes: legal should review any permanent data-access exceptions; we should involve Product Security early in the SOW. I'm ok to own security artifacts and the evidence pack but will need one engineer from Infra to help validate the signing flow during the pilot.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Jordan / all —

Infra perspective, top risks and notes:

1) Hardware image and drivers — customer wants NVMe + 2x A10G. We need to produce a validated appliance image (Ubuntu kernel + CUDA/cuDNN matrix). Risk: driver/kernel mismatch across Regal node models. Mitigator: define a supported hardware compatibility list (HCL) and provide a pre-flight hardware checklist; offer a small compatibility test bundle they can run.

2) On-call and support footprint — running an on-prem pilot requires 24/7 escalation window (even if limited) and a runbook for triage. Risk: we don't have dedicated on-prem SREs on the roster for Q2. Mitigator: propose a 90-day "managed pilot" fee that includes 0.25 FTE SRE time and scheduled weekly office hours.

3) Updates and rollback mechanics — offline updates require a robust rollback path and artifact provenance. Mitigator: we package updates as immutable bundles with checksums and provide a documented rollback command; test rollback in our staging images before handoff.

Operational ask: I'll need an infra dev (2 wks part-time) to assemble the appliance image and test the update flow. I'll also need a quick network diagram from Regal (their DBs, internal NAT, any proxy) to finalize firewall rules.

Attaching a quick sketch I drew from the alpha call (network_zone_sketch.png).

-Marcus

Jordan —

From runtime/serving side, short list:

1) Model compatibility and quantization — offline bundles must include model artifacts we have validated for offline execution; some of our latest large variants assume runtime kernels not available on older GPUs. Risk: performance regression or memory OOMs. Mitigator: offer a curated "offline model pack" (quantized INT8 where acceptable) and a compatibility matrix; if customer insists on a larger variant, propose reduced context or batching limits.

2) KV cache persistence and warm-starts — for an on-prem clinical assistant, warm cache matters to hit latency SLOs. Risk: cold starts causing poor UX. Mitigator: provide a save/restore tool for KV cache snapshots that the customer can load on restart; document safe snapshot cadence.

3) Local evals and quality monitoring — since telemetry is limited, we lose signal on regressions. Mitigator: include an embedded eval harness in the image that runs nightly checks and outputs aggregate metrics into the signed evidence pack; customer can choose to share or keep locally.

Operational asks: I need a dev (1 week) to produce the offline bundle builder and run a compatibility test against the A10G matrix Marcus will provide. Also need to lock the supported-model list for the pilot (I'd suggest: small Llama-variant quantized, and our mid-tier conversational model quantized to INT8).

-Karthik
